record.original_question: Given a tournament T, an integer k, and vertices x and y of T, must T contain two arc-disjoint spanning branchings: an in-arborescence rooted at x and an out-arborescence rooted at y, with each branching having at most k leaves? Equivalently, characterize or decide when a tournament admits arc-disjoint in- and out-branchings with prescribed roots and with both branchings having at most k leaves.

evidence.quote: given T a tournament, k an integer, x and y vertices of T, does T contain arc-disjoint in- and out-arborescences with roots x and y and both with at most k leaves ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A tournament is a directed graph $T=(V,A)$ obtained by orienting each edge of a complete undirected graph; equivalently, for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in V$ exactly one of the arcs $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ belongs to $A$. A spanning out-arborescence (out-branching) of $T$ rooted at a vertex $y$ is a spanning subdigraph $B^+\subseteq T$ that is a tree when its arcs are regarded as undirected edges, and in which every vertex except $y$ has exactly one entering arc (so there is a unique directed path from $y$ to every other vertex). A spanning in-arborescence (in-branching) of $T$ rooted at a vertex $x$ is defined analogously but with every vertex except $x$ having exactly one outgoing arc (so there is a unique directed path from every vertex to $x$). A leaf of a branching is a vertex whose out-degree (in the out-branching) or in-degree (in the in-branching) within the branching is zero. Two branchings are arc-disjoint if they share no arc.

Problem. Determine the computational complexity, and provide a structural characterization, of the following decision problem:

Input: a tournament $T$, two (not necessarily distinct) vertices $x,y\in V(T)$, and a non-negative integer $k$.

Question: does $T$ contain a spanning in-arborescence $B^-$ rooted at $x$ and a spanning out-arborescence $B^+$ rooted at $y$ such that $B^-$ and $B^+$ are arc-disjoint and each of $B^-$ and $B^+$ has at most $k$ leaves?
artifact.status_search_result: Without the leaf restriction, the existence of arc-disjoint in- and out-branchings with prescribed roots in a tournament (and more generally in semicomplete digraphs) is known to admit a polynomial-time decision algorithm (Bang-Jensen's conjecture, established for tournaments and extended to semicomplete digraphs in 2023). However, no characterization or complexity result was found for the variant where each branching is additionally required to have at most $k$ leaves; related parameterized problems (k-distinct branchings, branchings with many leaves) have been studied but do not resolve this specific question. The status therefore appears to be unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Arc-disjoint out-branchings and in-branchings in semicomplete digraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization for semicomplete digraphs having a pair of arc-disjoint branchings with prescribed roots, confirming a conjecture of Bang-Jensen.
status_evidence.claim: The unrestricted (no leaf bound) version is polynomially solvable for tournaments/semicomplete digraphs.

status_evidence.title: k-Distinct In- and Out-Branchings in Digraphs
status_evidence.snippet: FPT algorithm for k-distinct branchings; relates to out-branchings with many leaves.
status_evidence.claim: Related parameterized variants are studied but do not address the at-most-k-leaves arc-disjoint version in tournaments.

status_evidence.title: Arc-disjoint out-branching and in-branching (Open Problem Garden)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem entry on arc-disjoint branchings.
status_evidence.claim: Arc-disjoint branching problems are tracked as open problems; the specific k-leaves variant in tournaments is not reported as solved.
